verdict.rationale: Kintsugi runs its own background automation: once a connector is authorized it keeps transactions in sync, and it files and remits on a recurring schedule. These are fixed, built-in compliance workflows rather than automations a user can design, and there is no documented trigger or rule builder, scheduler, or agent-driven automation. The MCP server only reads docs and never calls the API. Missing for 10: user-configurable automation and workflow definitions, custom triggers and schedules, agent-executed background tasks, monitoring and controls for automated runs, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Pick your platform, authorize it once, and Kintsugi keeps transactions in sync from then on.
It watches where your sales create an obligation, prices the right rate at checkout, registers you in the jurisdictions that require it, and files and remits on schedule.
